$comment: [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OPERAND]] (P31, 2026-08-24) — the FIRST runnable witness that alignof accepts an EXPRESSION operand. ★★★ BORN AGAINST A REFUSAL, NOT A MISCOMPILE: ✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI at HEAD `60198126`, every value-form line in main.c failed the build with `error[P0009]` naming `AlignofKeyword` in the expected set, in all three spellings and in both the parenthesised and paren-free forms; ✔MEASURED the same day on gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 (`-std=gnu17`), all three compile this exact file and RUN it to 42. ★★ THE DISCRIMINATING SHAPES, each named because none of them is decoration: SHAPE 4 is `__alignof__(*p)` on a `char *`, where the two candidate lowerings answer 1 and 8 — the DIRECT operand stamp versus a DFS descent to the first stamped leaf — and the descent is not hypothetical, it is [[D-CSUBSET-SIZEOF-DEREF-ARRAY-SILENT-FALLBACK]], which mis-sized `sizeof(*p)`, under-allocated a pthread mutex and became a deterministic SIGABRT in a shipped SQLite; SHAPE 6 is a `char[3]`, the only shape here where alignof (1) and sizeof (3) DISAGREE, so it is the sole detector for a paste of the sizeof arm into the alignof one; SHAPE 7 is the TYPE form in an array dimension and a `_Static_assert`, which is a REGRESSION pin rather than a feature pin — adding the value arm moved `hirLowering.alignofRule` from the form to the new `alignofExpr` wrapper, and three consumers dispatch on that id, so a fix that taught only the lowering would leave `int a[_Alignof(double)]` failing S_NonConstantArrayLength while every new-feature test stayed green; SHAPE 8 is the VALUE form in those same const-expr positions, whose operand `*(double *)0` is legal precisely because the operand is UNEVALUATED (C 6.5.3.4p1). ★ THE `release` ARM: every check is an explicit early return, so the optimizer cannot turn a wrong answer into a right exit code; `dss_seed` is `volatile` so the final arithmetic keeps a real load and the exit code stays a FUNCTION of the measured values rather than a constant. ⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED: gcc reports the DECLARED alignment of an OVER-ALIGNED OBJECT while clang reports the TYPE alignment — the references disagree, so this file states nothing about it and the divergence is anchored at [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OVERALIGNED-OBJECT]] instead.
